title: How do we multiply by 101, 1001, 99 and 999 in one line?
description: A multiplier one more or one less than a round number turns each multiplication into a round number step plus or minus the number. Six multiplications are done and one is checked by adding back. Keeko doubts that ninety nine also adds the number.
teaching_notes: One idea: split the multiplier as a round number plus or minus one, then distribute. Watch for students who add the number for ninety nine, as they did for one hundred one.

video_script.why: The child has multiplied by one hundred one with the number shifted and added. Here the same idea covers one thousand one, ninety nine and nine hundred ninety nine.
video_script.substitution: Write the multiplier as a round number plus or minus one, multiply by the round number, then add or take away the number once.
video_script.anchor: six multiplications with multipliers close to round numbers
video_script.wrong_answer: put two zeros then add the number once more
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko puts two zeros and adds the number, as for one hundred one, and gets nine hundred eighty three thousand one hundred thirty four. That is too big by twice the number.
video_script.payoff_line: Split the multiplier into a round number plus or minus one

final_answer.spoken: eight thousand nine hundred eighty nine, ninety five thousand eight hundred forty nine, two hundred sixty six million ninety six thousand eight hundred thirty one, one million one hundred twelve thousand one hundred eleven, nine hundred sixty three thousand six hundred sixty six, and twenty three million four hundred fifty four thousand five hundred twenty two

never_show: ninety nine done by adding the number, marked as right
maths_rules: adding instead of taking away gives 973400 + 9734 = 983134, which is 19468 too big
video_script.design: One idea: the multiplier is a round number plus or minus one, so the number is added or taken away once. Uses the method of the times one hundred one video. Wrong idea: ninety nine also adds the number. The six lines stay on the board through the doubt.

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, for times one hundred one, put two zeros after the number, then add the number.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Eighty nine becomes eight thousand nine hundred, plus eighty nine.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Nine hundred forty nine works the same way.

beats.colours: the added number in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, for times one thousand one, put three zeros after the number, then add the number.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Two hundred sixty five thousand eight hundred thirty one gets three zeros, then the number is added.
<bookmark mark='b'/>One thousand one hundred eleven works the same way.

beats.colours: the taken away number in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, ninety nine is one hundred minus one.
Put two zeros after the number, then take the number away.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Nine thousand seven hundred thirty four gives nine hundred seventy three thousand four hundred, minus the number.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Twenty three thousand four hundred seventy eight times nine hundred ninety nine works the same way.

marks.back: 963666 + 9734 = 973400 is written, matching the first row

narration: <bookmark mark='res'/>Step four, check ninety nine by adding the number back.
Nine hundred sixty three thousand six hundred sixty six, plus nine thousand seven hundred thirty four.
<bookmark mark='back'/>That is nine hundred seventy three thousand four hundred, as it should be.

<bookmark mark='a4'/>Then nine hundred sixty three thousand six hundred sixty six.

beats.colours: the wrong bubble in the warning colour
narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks put two zeros then add the number once more, as for one hundred one.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it on nine thousand seven hundred thirty four.
Adding gives nine hundred eighty three thousand one hundred thirty four.
That is too big by twice the number.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Ninety nine is one less than one hundred, so the number is taken away, not added.
